info.title: EsignCenter API
info.description: The EsignCenter REST API: create templates, send documents for signature and read the results from your own code. Authenticate with an X-Auth-Token header; API access is on the paid plan.

tags.name: Submissions
tags.description: Signature requests can be initiated with Submissions API. Submissions can contain one submitter if signed by a single party or multiple submitters if the document template form contains signatures and fields to be collected and filled by multiple parties. Initiate new submissions to request signatures for specified submitters via email or phone number.

tags.name: Template Builder Sessions
tags.description: Embedded template builder sessions for CRM-style document workflows.

tags.name: Signing Sessions
tags.description: Signing Sessions create embeddable signing flows for another application while keeping API tokens on the server side.

tags.name: Submitters
tags.description: Submitters API allows you to load all details provided by the signer of the document.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Templates represent reusable document signing forms with fields and signatures to be collected. Create one from a PDF or image your application generates with POST /templates, or build it in the web app and reuse it from the API.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The user an API token belongs to.

tags.name: Template Preview Sessions
tags.description: Read-only embedded previews with synthetic values; no signing submission is created.

post.summary: Create a template from a PDF
post.description: The API endpoint provides the functionality to create a reusable, signable template from documents your application generates. Send each file base64-encoded, and optionally the signing parties and where each field goes. PDF and image files only - Word, Excel and HTML are not accepted here. Leave `fields` out and the fillable form fields already present in the PDF are detected and used. Send `fields` and detection is skipped: the fields are placed exactly where the `areas` coordinates put them. A `template.created` webhook is delivered to every endpoint subscribed to it - see the API and webhooks guide.

name.description: Name of the template. Defaults to the file name of the first document.

external_id.description: Your application-specific identifier for this template, returned on the template and usable as a filter on `GET /templates`. `application_key` is accepted as an alias.

folder_name.description: Name of the folder to create the template in. The folder is created if it does not exist yet.

documents.description: The files the template is built from. At least one, up to 20.

name.description: Name of the document. Defaults to document-1.pdf, document-2.pdf and so on.

file.description: Base64-encoded PDF or image file, up to 25MB once decoded. Word, Excel and HTML files are refused with a 422.

submitters.description: The signing parties. Names must be unique. Defaults to a single party named 'First Party'.

fields.description: Where the fields go. Leave this out to use the fillable fields already in the PDF.

role.description: Name of the submitter who fills this field. Must match one of the `submitters` names; the first submitter is used when it is omitted.

required.description: Indicates if the field is required.

readonly.description: Indicates if the field is filled in advance and cannot be changed by the signer.

title.description: Field title shown on the signing form instead of the name.

description.description: Field description shown on the signing form.

default_value.description: Value the field is pre-filled with. A string, or an array for fields that take several values.

preferences.description: Field appearance preferences (font size, font, colour, alignment), as returned in the template response.

options.description: Choices for 'radio', 'multiple' and 'select' fields. Required for 'radio' and 'multiple', which also need one area per option.

value.description: The option shown to the signer.

areas.description: Where the field is placed. Coordinates are fractions of the page between 0 and 1, not pixels.

x.description: Distance of the left edge of the field box from the left edge of the page, as a fraction of the page width.

y.description: Distance of the top edge of the field box from the top of the page, as a fraction of the page height.

w.description: Width of the field box, as a fraction of the page width.

h.description: Height of the field box, as a fraction of the page height.

page.description: Page the field box is on. The first page is 0.

document.description: Index of the uploaded document the field box is on, in the order the documents were sent. The first document is 0.

cell_w.description: Width of a single character cell, for the 'cells' field type.

option.description: For 'radio' and 'multiple' fields, the option this box belongs to: the option's value, or its 0-based index. Each option needs its own box.

post.description: This API endpoint allows you to create signature requests (submissions) for a document template and send them to the specified submitters (signers).

template_id.description: The unique identifier of the template. Document template forms can be created via the Web UI, PDF and DOCX API, or HTML API.

send_email.description: Set `false` to disable signature request emails sending.

send_sms.description: Set `true` to send signature request via phone number and SMS.

order.description: Pass 'random' to send signature request emails to all parties right away. The order is 'preserved' by default so the second party will receive a signature request email only after the document is signed by the first party.

completed_redirect_url.description: Specify URL to redirect to after the submission completion.

bcc_completed.description: Specify BCC address to send signed documents to after the completion.

reply_to.description: Specify Reply-To address to use in the notification emails.

expire_at.description: Specify the expiration date and time after which the submission becomes unavailable for signature.

body.description: Custom signature request email body. Can include the following variables: {{template.name}}, {{submitter.link}}, {{account.name}}.

submitters.description: The list of submitters for the submission.

role.description: The role name or title of the submitter.

email.description: The email address of the submitter.

phone.description: The phone number of the submitter, formatted according to the E.164 standard.

values.description: An object with pre-filled values for the submission. Use field names for keys of the object. For more configurations see `fields` param.

external_id.description: Your application-specific unique string key to identify this submitter within your app.

completed.description: Pass `true` to mark submitter as completed and auto-signed via API. No ESIGN consent is collected or recorded for such a submitter — your application is responsible for the signer's consent to sign electronically; the audit trail marks this completion as made via API.

metadata.description: Metadata object with additional submitter information.

send_email.description: Set `false` to disable signature request emails sending only for this submitter.

send_sms.description: Set `true` to send signature request via phone number and SMS.

reply_to.description: Specify Reply-To address to use in the notification emails for this submitter.

completed_redirect_url.description: Submitter specific URL to redirect to after the submission completion.

order.description: The order of the submitter in the workflow (e.g., 0 for the first signer, 1 for the second, etc.). Use the same order number to create order groups. By default, submitters are ordered as in the submitters array.

require_email_2fa.description: Set to `true` to require email 2FA verification via a one-time code sent to the email address in order to access the documents. Phone (SMS) verification is not offered: a truthy `require_phone_2fa` is rejected with 422 — use `require_email_2fa` instead.

subject.description: Custom signature request email subject for the submitter.

body.description: Custom signature request email body for the submitter. Can include the following variables: {{template.name}}, {{submitter.link}}, {{account.name}}.

fields.description: A list of configurations for template document form fields.

default_value.description: Default value of the field. Use base64 encoded file or a public URL to the image file to set default signature or image fields.

readonly.description: Set `true` to make it impossible for the submitter to edit predefined field value.

required.description: Set `true` to make the field required.

title.description: Field title displayed to the user instead of the name, shown on the signing form. Supports Markdown.

description.description: Field description displayed on the signing form. Supports Markdown.

pattern.description: HTML field validation pattern string based on https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/pattern specification.

message.description: A custom error message to display on validation failure.

min.description: Minimum allowed number value or date depending on field type.

max.description: Maximum allowed number value or date depending on field type.

step.description: Increment step for number field. Pass 1 to accept only integers, or 0.01 to accept decimal currency.

font_size.description: Font size of the field value in pixels.

font_type.description: Font type of the field value.

font.description: Font family of the field value.

color.description: Font color of the field value.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of the field text value.

valign.description: Vertical alignment of the field text value.

format.description:
The data format for different field types.
- Date field: accepts formats such as DD/MM/YYYY (default: MM/DD/YYYY).
- Signature field: accepts drawn, typed, drawn_or_typed (default), or upload.
- Number field: accepts currency formats such as usd, eur, gbp.

price.description: Price value of the payment field. Only for payment fields.

currency.description: Currency value of the payment field. Only for payment fields.

mask.description: Set `true` to make sensitive data masked on the document.

reasons.description: An array of signature reasons to choose from.

roles.description: A list of roles for the submitter. Use this param to merge multiple roles into one submitter.

email.description: The email address of the submitter.

slug.description: Unique key to be used in the signing form URL.

status.description: The status of signing request for the submitter.

values.description: An array of pre-filled values for the submission.

sent_at.description: The date and time when the signing request was sent to the submitter.

opened_at.description: The date and time when the submitter opened the signing form.

completed_at.description: The date and time when the submitter completed the signing form.

declined_at.description: The date and time when the submitter declined the signing form.

created_at.description: The date and time when the submitter was created.

updated_at.description: The date and time when the submitter was last updated.

phone.description: The phone number of the submitter.

external_id.description: Your application-specific unique string key to identify this submitter within your app.

send_email.description: Indicates whether the signature request email should be sent.

send_sms.description: Indicates whether the signature request should be sent via SMS.

role.description: The role of the submitter in the signing process.

embed_src.description: The `src` URL value to embed the signing form or sign via a link.

post.summary: Create an embeddable template builder session
post.description: Creates a short-lived embedded template builder URL for a CRM or another app. The session can open an existing template, clone a saved template, clone and replace documents, or create a new template from base64 PDF/image documents. Keep the X-Auth-Token on your backend and pass only builder_src to the frontend.

template_id.description: Existing template ID to open in the embedded builder. Send this by itself, without clone_template_id or documents.

get.description: The API endpoint returns the user the API token belongs to. It is the cheapest way to check that a token works: every other endpoint in this reference acts on that user's account. A valid token on an account whose plan does not include the API is refused here with 403, like every other endpoint - a 403 means the plan, not the token.

401.description: Unauthorized - no token was presented, the token is not a token of this instance, or the account it belongs to is no longer active.

403.description: Forbidden - the API is not included in this account's plan. The token itself is valid.

post.summary: Create a read-only embedded template preview
post.description: Creates an expiring iframe URL for a template owned by the API account without creating a submission or signer. Paid customer and internal integration accounts may use it. The preview and its consent PDF are revoked when the account is suspended, archived, or loses embedding access. Keep the API token on the server. Use synthetic values: the signed URL payload is readable.

embed_origin.description: Exact HTTPS origin allowed to frame the preview; localhost HTTP is permitted in development.

values.description: Synthetic sample values keyed by field name or UUID; maximum 4096 bytes serialized JSON. Unknown and attachment-backed fields are ignored.

id.description: Signed preview token, also returned as token.

preview_src.description: Expiring bearer URL to iframe; share only with authorized viewers.

403.description: Account inactive or embedding not entitled
